headline: Highest risk is Continue’s filesystem/MCP reach interacting with Whisper’s CLI-only, no-network profile; prompt-injection and leakage are limited by the pair’s lack of direct shared channels.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Continue can read workspace files and use MCP, so if Whisper outputs are manually copied into files or prompts, malicious text could influence Continue. Whisper itself has no clipboard, network, or MCP surface, so the bridge is indirect and user-mediated rather than automatic.
conditions: IF Whisper output is pasted into a file or prompt that Continue reads
IF an MCP server exposed to Continue forwards untrusted text from Whisper
mitigations: Keep Whisper outputs out of prompt-bearing files
Use a dedicated scratch file for transcription review
Disable MCP servers that relay untrusted text
Require manual review before copying transcripts into Continue

B_data_leakage.rationale: Continue touches source code and open editor buffers and can write the filesystem, while Whisper touches audio files only and has no network egress. There is no documented shared workspace or automatic upload path between them, so leakage is possible mainly through operator-managed file transfer, not default cross-agent exposure.
conditions: IF audio transcripts are copied into the same workspace as source code
IF Continue is pointed at files containing sensitive audio-derived text
mitigations: Store audio and code in separate directories
Avoid pasting transcripts into shared project files
Review workspace permissions before opening in Continue
Delete temporary transcript files after use

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Continue has filesystem write access and shared state via filesystem across IDE windows, but Whisper is not runnable and has no filesystem write capability. Because both do not write the same mutable resource by default, direct capability conflict is limited to unusual orchestration or manual file handoff.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator gives both agents write access to the same directory
IF Whisper transcripts are written into files that Continue edits concurrently
mitigations: Separate writable directories per agent
Serialize edits to shared files
Use read-only mounts for Whisper outputs
Avoid concurrent writes to the same workspace

D_cascading_error.rationale: Continue can act on workspace content, but Whisper is a speech model with no tool use or downstream action authority. Any cascade requires the operator to treat Whisper transcripts as authoritative and then let Continue act on them, so the pathway exists only through manual workflow, not an autonomous chain.
conditions: IF Whisper transcripts are used as authoritative instructions or facts
IF Continue is allowed to modify files based on those transcripts without review
mitigations: Require human verification of transcripts before action
Mark transcripts as untrusted input
Use a review step before file edits
Limit Continue to suggestion-only mode where possible

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance mismatch is evidenced in the profiles: Continue is open-source with no stated residency or retention constraints, and Whisper is open-source and non-runnable with no data residency claims. The pair does not document PHI, EU PII, or retention-policy conflicts, so a compliance breach pathway is not established.
conditions: IF either agent is deployed under an external policy not shown in the profiles
IF sensitive regulated data is introduced into the workflow
mitigations: Document data-class handling before deployment
Add a retention policy for transcripts
Review vendor compliance claims separately
Keep regulated data out of the pair until policies are confirmed
